projects.title: JIESHIN TSENG
projects.materials: Paper remnants, found objects, tissue-paper casts, site fragments
projects.summary: A bilingual living archive that turns studio research into a discoverable public practice — so curators, tutors and collaborators can find the work, the process, and a clear path to contact.

pitch.hook: From private studio notes to a public artist presence that institutions can actually navigate.
pitch.challenge: Jieshin’s practice spans sculpture, installation, painting and writing between London and Taiwan — but the work lived as scattered folders, Instagram fragments and closed studio notes. For a degree-show year and residency cycle, that made the practice hard to brief, hard to cite, and hard to commission.
pitch.influence: The website positions 曾潔心 as the hero of the story. Instead of a generic gallery template, we built an indexed archive that makes material research legible: titles, years, process writing and installation images sit in one bilingual system. Email and Instagram stay one tap away, so interest converts into conversation — for tutors, curators, pop-up hosts and future residencies.
features: Split archive: numbered works list + live media stage
Bilingual artist identity (EN / 中文) from the first viewport
Project pages with process writing and image sequences
About as a living studio statement, not a static bio block
Direct enquiry paths: Email + Instagram CTAs
Mobile-first index for fast scanning at shows and studio visits
Image-heavy Next.js delivery tuned for portfolio performance
outcomes: 20+ works (2020–2026) organised as a navigable archive
Degree show, Dilston residency and pop-ups documented as chapters
Clear bilingual brand surface for international discovery
A durable home for process — not only finished installation shots

projects.title: FRED'S CAFE
projects.summary: Neighbourhood website for Fred's Community Cafe in Crofton Park — Allpress coffee, garden suntrap, events and local gatherings opposite the station.

pitch.hook: A neighbourhood cafe site that makes Allpress coffee, the garden suntrap and local gatherings easy to find.
pitch.challenge: Fred’s Community Cafe opposite Crofton Park station needed a clear digital front door — hours, menu cues, events and a sense of place without a corporate template.
pitch.influence: The site holds Brockley Road identity in one place so regulars and newcomers can plan a visit, check the garden, and stay close to community programming.

Space for events and neighbourhood gatherings
outcomes: A durable home for Fred’s online presence
